subject.title: feat(feeds): refresh and manage followed publishers

question: Should OpenClaw core own a persistent signed-publisher follow service with Gateway RPCs and a background refresh scheduler, or should this remain an external/plugin or ClawHub integration behind existing generic seams?
rationale: The patch creates durable public protocol, CLI, storage, scheduling, and trust-boundary contracts; code review cannot determine the intended permanent product and ownership boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the core control plane
options.body: Confirm core ownership, then require public contract documentation and configured-Gateway proof before considering merge.

options.title: Keep publisher workflow external
options.body: Direct the work to a plugin or ClawHub-owned package and avoid adding publisher-specific RPCs, scheduler state, and CLI commands to core.

recommendation.title: Keep publisher workflow external
recommendation.body: Direct the work to a plugin or ClawHub-owned package and avoid adding publisher-specific RPCs, scheduler state, and CLI commands to core.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed contributor spanning the related publisher-feed implementation stack; a repository owner should make the final product decision.
